utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there are no preliminaries, which means that the witness can be escorted into the courtroom. No protective measures. You're ready, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At this time, the Prosecution seeks leave to call Nedzib Djozo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'll use the time while waiting for the witness for the following. During Idriz Merdjanic's testimony on the 1st of October of this year, D59 was MFI'd because the translation states that the document concerned a handwritten note and the original document does not reflect that. On the 12th of October, the parties informed the Chamber that they are discussing D59, and the Chamber would like to remind both parties that it is waiting for the final version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djozo. Before you give evidence, the Rules require --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, the text of which is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djozo. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, you'll first by examined by Mr. Weber. Mr. Weber is counsel for the Prosecution and you'll find him to your right. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please introduce yourself to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: My name is Nedzib Djozo. I was born on the 4th of May, 1958, in Datelji. I live in Sarajevo on Sulejman Filipovic Street number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, did you provide statements to the Office of the Prosecutor in November 1995 and April 2005?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Have you testified before this Tribunal on three previous occasions in the cases of Prosecutor versus Dragomir Milosevic, Prosecutor versus Perisic, and most recently, Prosecutor versus Karadzic in December 2010?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Prior to your Karadzic testimony, did you provide a third statement consolidating and clarifying evidence you presented in past statements and testimony?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please display page 1 of 65 ter 28557 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the document before you as the amalgamated statement you provided on 7 December 2010, prior to your testimony in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on the bottom of this page?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you have any corrections to the spelling of your place of birth that is before you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. As my place of birth, it reads Dartalje, whereas the correct spelling should be Datelji, D-a-t-e-l-j-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 14 of the English version of this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, did you sign this page after the statement was read back to you in the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have and opportunity to review this statement in a language you understand prior to your testimony here today?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you were asked questions similar to the ones posed to you in the past, would you provide similar answers as reflected in this statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Now that you've taken the solemn declaration in this case, do you affirm the truthfulness of this statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 28557 into evidence as a public exhibit. We also tender at this time two associated exhibits, 65 ter 19725 and 19775 as public exhibits. These are discussed in paragraph 21 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 28557 becomes Exhibit P544.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P544 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19725 becomes Exhibit P545, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P545 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And document 19775 becomes Exhibit P546, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P546 is admitted. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: With the Chamber's leave, the Prosecution at this time seeks permission to present a public summary of Mr. Djozo's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During the war, Mr. Djozo served as a police officer for the Sarajevo Police Department in the Stari Grad or Old Town police station from July 1992 onward. In his capacity as a police investigator, he investigated shelling and sniping cases. Mr. Djozo conducted a number of on-site investigations concerning the wounding and killing of civilians in Sedrenik, a residential area under the responsibility of his police station. In these investigations, he found that there was fire coming from the Bosnian Serb-held territory, in particular the sniping location of Spicasta Stijena, which is a hill overlooking the Sedrenik neighbourhood. In the months immediately before the shelling of the Markale marketplace on 28 August 1995, Mr. Djozo investigated several incidents of mortar impacts in the immediate vicinity. On the day of 28 August 1995, he attended the site of the Markale incident. During the course of his investigations, Mr. Djozo encountered other explosive devices that were used against or fired on Sarajevo. He investigated a modified air bomb that fell in the canyon of the Moscanice river without exploding. He found that the projectile was an air bomb with four rocket motors attached to it. Mr. Djozo also saw gas containers filled with explosives which were rolled down into the city from Bosnian Serb-held territories on the slopes of Mount Trebevic beneath Osmica. May I proceed, Your Honours, with the questioning of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, can you approximate for us how many shells fell upon the Stari Grad area of Sarajevo between 1992 and 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I cannot give you even an approximate number. I can only say that there were thousands upon thousands of shells that fell on the Stari Grad area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Between 1992 and 1995, were there any weapons placements or any military locations located within the Stari Grad area?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The only location where there was army present, and that was the Yugoslav People's Army, was in the area of Bistrik where the command of the 7th Military District or army district was stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was the address of the Stari Grad police station?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The street where the police station was located is called Logavina Street, and it was at number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please describe the Stari Grad police station and the buildings that immediately surround it.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The Stari Grad police station was housed in a building with a basement, ground floor, first floor, and attic. There were residential buildings the police station that were two- or three-storeys high.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please display page 15 of 65 ter 10264. It is a photograph. There is no translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the area depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What do you recognise this area to be?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: In the foreground we can see private homes that form part of the Sedrenik neighbourhood, and in the background one can see the feature called Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does this photograph accurately depict the Sedrenik area as it appeared during the war?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Court Officer please provide the witness with a pen to mark the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 16 of your statement, you state: "Spicasta Stijena is a hill dominant overlooking the Sedrenik neighbourhood. Spicasta Stijena was under the control of the members of the Army of Republika Srpska. Spicasta Stijena was a well-known aggressor-held sniping place." Is this sniping position visible in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please take the pen and mark the location of the sniping position with the letter S.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please draw a box around what you've described as the Sedrenik neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution tenders the photograph at this time as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The photograph marked by the witness would receive, Madam Registrar, what number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P547 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know whether people were cutting trees down near the area of Spicasta Stijena for firewood?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there any particular months in which they would do this?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: They would mostly cut trees just ahead of the winter, because they needed wood for heating.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 10105 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this Official Note dated 12 March 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 2 of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does your signature appear on this page?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review this Official Note during proofing yesterday?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to this Official Note, a woman described to you how she was shot while going to get firewood on 10 December 1994 in Sedrenik. Based on your review of this Official Note, does it accurately reflect your interview of this woman who was wounded?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 10105 as a public exhibit. We did check, and it is okay to tender publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10105 becomes Exhibit P548, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P548 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 19775 for the witness. I apologise. I just read out the wrong number. It's 19776.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you is a cover page of one of two notebooks which is entitled "Stari Grad SJB Sarajevo. War Diary." Do you recognise the name of the person on this cover page?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Who is this person?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Chief of the Stari Grad public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to review those notebooks during proofing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware of these notebooks while you were employed at the Stari Grad SJB?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what the entries in these notebooks relate to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Most of the entries in this war diary related to the places that were the source of shelling in the Bosnian Serb-controlled area, place and date, time, those wounded or injured and killed, civilians, in the area covered by the Stari Grad police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does it include any information related to incidents where individuals were shot at?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Of course. The entries also include sniping incidents, incidents where there was gunfire from infantry weapons and the so-called death mowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Death sowers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to go through a couple entries with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have the bottom of page 23 of the English translation and the middle of page 71 of the B/C/S copy. For reference the entry the Prosecution will be referring to in the English translation continues on to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the entry for 27 April 1993, under the location of Bascarsija, which indicates a N. Djozo was wounded by a shell, do you know what this entry relates to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I do. This was on Branilaca Sarajeva street. At the time it was called the JNA street, where Naim Djozo, a person by the name of Hasic, and another unidentified person were killed. Naim Djozo is my brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was your bothering doing when he was wounded on this day?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: He was an electrician by trade, and he was on his way to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 72 of the English translation and page 231 of the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the entry for 27/28 May 1992 under the location of Hrid-Jarcedoli. This entry mentions a number of areas including Pogledine, Kamenice, Mahmutovac, and Colina Kapa which were targeted from all available artillery pieces. Are these areas all located in Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. They are the neighbourhoods of the Stari Grad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 104 of the English translation and page 337 of the B/C/S original.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the entry for 2 July 1992 under Vratnik that describes about 400 people of Muslim nationality arriving in Vratnik from Pale. Are you familiar with what is described in this entry?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Members of the Army of Republika Srpska informed our superiors that at Vratnik there was a large number of Muslims who had been expelled from Pale. Policemen were supposed to go to meet them there and bring them into town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know any of the individuals who are amongst the people that were expelled from Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. This group included my relatives who lived in Pale, my aunt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were all the people that were expelled on this occasion originally from the municipality of Pale?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Before the war, the municipality of Pale was one of the city municipalities and it covered a large territory, roughly 50 to 60 kilometres towards Gorazde, Sokolac, Olovo. And all of these persons -- and actually, this list does not include all the ethnic Muslims who were expelled from that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 3 of the English translation and page 7 of the B/C/S original. In the English translation, if we could please scroll to the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the entry for 13/14 December 1992 that states the police commander of the Hrid-Jarcedoli police station killed himself with an M-70 automatic rifle. Do you know what happened before this police station commander killed himself?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. The commander was our colleague who had lost his entire family a few days before that. A shell that was fired from these Chetnik positions killed his wife and two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 21 of the English translation and page 63 of the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to the entry for 17/18 April 1993, under Sedrenik that indicates a 13-year-old girl was lightly wounded by the "sower of death" which you have previously mentioned now during your testimony. Since this is one of many entries in these notebooks that refer to the sower of death, could you please explain to us what this reference is to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Sower of death probably has a different name as well, a technical name, but this is an automatic weapon that has immense firing power. It's a recent thing. I did my military service in the JNA in 1980, and I did not come across this weapon. Basically amongst us we said, and perhaps that is actually the case, that when this weapon is fired, as a bullet leaves the barrel the next bullet is in the middle of the barrel, and the third bullet is also fired and in the barrel at the same time. So that shows how fast bullets are fired from this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were there multiple locations where civilians in Sarajevo were fired upon by this type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Of course. There is not a single part of the city of Sarajevo that was not fired at from this weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know where a sower of death-type weapon was located in relation to the Sedrenik neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Well, when the aggression was launched against Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Chetniks -- or, rather, the Army of Republika Srpska took all the elevations around Sarajevo and around the old town. So basically on every elevation there was a weapon like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Previously we looked at a photograph where you marked a letter S in an area that you've identified as a sniping location on a hill in Spicasta Stijena. Do you know where there was a sower of death in relation to this location that you marked?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I marked only one location from which a sniper operated, where we had located it. However, Spicasta Stijena is an area that covers a large part of the Sedrenik area, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Consultations during the break. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could continue with your answer as you've been provided it, or if you'd like me to repeat the question, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I shall continue. So Spicasta Stijena is one part. It's an elevation, an area where the lines of the Army of Republika Srpska were. From these trenches, and there were quite a few of them, small arms were opened, death sowers and snipers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 19776 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we do so, could I take the witness back to one of the pages of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 24 in English, 71 in B/C/S. Witness, I am referring to the entry which you said was about your brother being wounded. You'll find it at the -- under the Bascarsija entry. In English what is written below reads: "All wounded at the Dom Ljiljana." Could you tell us is that the place where these persons were wounded, hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dom Ljiljana is in the Branilaca Sarajeva Street. They were all wounded in that street by that building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To the extent you know, were they wounded outside that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what is written here, that they were wounded by that building. That is to say that they were outdoors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that your brother was on his way to work. What was the job of your brother?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An electrician, a repairman. He repairs electricity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. He did not or did he perform his job on that day at the BH Army Social Centre as it is written here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was employed in a company called unioninvest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but was he -- at that moment was he doing his job in or -- in relation to that building, or was he just passing by, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was passing by this building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections against the admission of the document just referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Well, we wouldn't object to the portions that were used, but to accept the whole document as this one only on the basis of several questions, we do object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the testimony of the witness also identified and authenticated the document as the one he knew, that's at least what I understand from his testimony, and the Chamber understands from his testimony, the objection is denied. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19776 becomes Exhibit P549, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P549 is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 19774.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the events that are described in this report?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In paragraph 25 of your statement which has now been admitted, you describe your participation in an on-site investigation into a shelling that occurred approximately a month before the Markale II incident, which happened on Dzenetica Cikma Street. Does this report relate to this same on-site investigation that you described in your statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the heading of the document the date indicated is 26 May 1995. The first line of the report says it was created on the 26th of June, 1995. There are multiple references in the body of this report to the shelling occurring on the 25th of June and the on-site investigation being conducted on the 26th. Could you please clarify the date of the shelling, the date that the shelling occurred.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The shelling occurred on the 25th of June, 1995, in the afternoon hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on that answer, then, is the date in the heading a typographical error?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The on-site investigation was carried out on the following day, in the morning, on the 26th of June, 1995. Probably it was impossible to carry it out because children had been killed or seriously wounded, and it could not have been completed properly during the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm just going to ask you to focus on the question. There seems to be, Mr. Weber, the date on this document is the 26th of the fifth month. Is that -- is that a mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, that is certainly a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It almost goes without saying, Mr. Weber, unless there's any reason to assume that someone has intentionally backdated it, so therefore even the Chamber would understand this to be a typographical -- a clerical error. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution tenders 65 ter 19774 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19774 becomes Exhibit P550, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P550 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 23137 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the drawing that is before you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you make this drawing?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you sign it and date the page that is before you, in the lower right corner?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what is depicted in this drawing.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This is a sketch of the location where children were fired upon and killed in the street of Dzenetica Cikma.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does it relate to the same incident which we just looked at in that report and which you also describe in your statement?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, before proceeding with the next question, I just wanted to -- and I apologise to the Chamber for this. With respect to the last document, P550, there maybe an issue of protective measures related to that. I'd ask that it be changed from public to under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is the street name that is towards the top of the drawing called Petrarkina Street? Did I say that correctly?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Petrarkina Street. That's its name, Petrarkina Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the former name of this street?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It was called Petrarkina, but I don't know what it's called nowadays.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Between Petrarkina and street and Dzenetica Cikma Street, there are three small star shapes. What do these represent?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It is approximately in these locations that the shells exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the bottom left hand of this drawing there is another small star-shaped symbol above the words "Markale Trznica." What does this star represent?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The explosion that took place in August 1995 when many citizens of Sarajevo were killed. It's Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the approximate distance between the location where the incident occurred on Dzenetica Cikma Street and the location where Markale II incident took place? If you could, if you could approximate in metres.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Approximately 50 metres or 20, 30, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time the Prosecution tenders 65 ter 23137 as a public exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 23137 becomes Exhibit P551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P551 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 11724. If for the time being it could please not be broadcast to the public. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's 65 ter 19724.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the official report is before you now?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This official report refers to on-site investigations into seven shellings that occurred on 1 July 1995. Did you participate in any of these investigations?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This was shelling here in Stari Grad centre, and I took part in some of the on-site investigations that were covered by the public security station of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the paragraph that indicates: "... the on-site investigation team was joined by Djozo Nedzib, SJB, Stari Grad operative worker." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the on-site investigations that are described in the paragraphs following the mention of your name in this report?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about two of the shellings that are described after the mention of your name. Approximately what was the distance between the location where a mortar projectile landed on Branilaca Grada Street on 1415 hours and the location where a mortar landed at Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street at 1430? Again, if you can approximate in metres.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It's the street nearby, so the distance is not more than 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Where are these two locations related in relation to where the mortar hit the Markale marketplace on 28 August 1995?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: In the street of Mula Mustafe Baseskije is the market in front of which this shell fell. The distance from this shell that fell on the 1st of July, 1995, at 1400 hours to the place where it fell on the 28th of August, 1995, it's not more than 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, before we continue, I am looking at the clock. You had a time estimate of one hour. Seven minutes are left from that. Do you think that you would finish in those seven minutes? Then we could consider to take the break slightly later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I was going to tender this document and ask one last question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution at this time tender 65 ter 19724 under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19724 becomes Exhibit P552 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted as such. That means under seal, under this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, in paragraph 35 of your statement, you state: "My view regarding these and other shellings, which was shared by others at the police station, is that the fire was adjusted until they reached the very crowded Markale to cause a big number of casualties." When you refer to these and other shellings, what other shellings are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, the shelling that ensued across Sarajevo mostly targeted the areas where citizens, children, firefighters, and paramedics would gather. So, for instance, on Vase Miskina Street, it was the line for bread. Next to Pivara or the brewery there was a line for water. Children sledding at Alipasino Polje. The sports match at Dobrinja. They specifically targeted the locations where a larger number of citizens would gather. In the Stari Grad area, it was precisely these spots that were targeted; namely Markale, the open-air marketplace at Mula Mustafe Baseskije Street, the closed-in marketplace at the entrance to which people would mill around on their way in or on their way out shopping for food to live on. All the citizens of Sarajevo, as well as others, know that this was done deliberately. Of course, the media of the Republika Srpska did everything in their power to persuade the international community above all and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. This goes well beyond your question. Therefore, if you would have addressed that matter that would have been different, but the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That was my last question. I would just make a note if we are going to break, we haven't received notice of the cross-documents, and it would be of assistance so we could print them out and look them over during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we'll do is the following: First, Mr. Djozo, we'll take a break, and we'd like you to see you back after that break. Could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We then move into private session for a short moment, and meanwhile we perhaps hear from Mr. Lukic whether the documents to be used in cross-examination are already communicated to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break and will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, as matters stand now, what is your time estimate? For the remainder of the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Leaving some time for the Prosecution, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Djozo, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic, and you'll find him over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djozo.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we start?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will start with some general questions first. From your statement, we know where you worked before June 1991 when you became a policeman. Before you became a policeman, did you complete any training or schooling, or were you simply mobilised?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I joined the police force voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you work as a policeman until mid-1994. I apologise, but I'm waiting for interpretation to finish. Then you move on to take the duties of an investigator in the crime police department. In the meantime, that is to say from the time you joined the police force and the time you took up these duties, did you complete any schooling?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. We had training and courses in the police station, or more precisely, in the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Up until 1992, you performed a duty which had nothing to do whatsoever with weapons; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As a member of the police force, you became a member of the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did you not?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You explained to us that you were a gunner in a mortar platoon and a site setter. Can you tell us on how many occasions were you handling a mortar?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I joined the Yugoslav People's Army in 1980. I had training in Banja Luka, and at that point I was immediately assigned to the post of a site setter or gunner in charge of a mortar. I was given the rank of lance corporal first and then corporal, and I was the commander or the leader of a platoon. Let me just complete my answer. In the training I undertook first, we went through live ammunition target practice, and then since I was there receiving two more generations of recruits, I therefore went through two more live ammunition target practices.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what was the mortar you were trained for?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: 82-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your earlier testimony, they asked you if you knew what the range of fire of a 120-millimetre mortar was, and your answer at the time was that you didn't know. Is that still the case? Do you still not know what the range of a 120-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, I don't know the range of a 120-millimetre mortar, but I do know very well that that it is 4.800 metres in the case of an 82-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 8 of your statement, you say that you were wounded close to the police station.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. I was wounded at the front door practically to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will come back to this and other cases when we will be establishing the direction of fire. I would now like to move on to another part of your statement. You don't have the statement before you, do you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can the statement be provided to the witness for me by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Prosecution has a spare copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm providing it to the Court Officer. For the record, we provided the B/C/S translation only. Not the signed version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Paragraphs are there, so that should be no problem. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at paragraph 12. It speaks about investigations into sniping and shelling incidents. In fact, it starts before paragraph 9. There you explain what your job was, and I mean in paragraph 12. You were not able to substitute for either a ballistics expert or a forensic officer in terms of their expertise.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Of course. They were experts in their own field and were the only ones who were competent to address them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were not authorised to engage into any evaluation of the type of ammunition retrieved at the crime scene; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It was the domain of the ballistics expert who would tell us what sort of shell or bullet was involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Likewise, you weren't entitled to assess what sort of projectile was involved in the shelling incidents; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Estimates could have been given by anyone, but the only document that carried validity was the one produced by the ballistics officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Moreover, you were not entitled to nor was this part of your duties to determine the direction of fire in the case of a shell or a bullet; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It was always done by the ballistics officer who was a member of the on-site investigation team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 14. You also explain what you were doing there, and you say that one of the important documents that you produced was the Official Note. Who had the right from among those who were in your police station to draft these official notes?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: If a duty operative officer or an inspector was present in the police station, he was duty-bound to produce a record of the on-site investigation, and an Official Note was a document which could be part of that report. The Official Note was produced by authorised officials, and they would send the note to the operative officer in charge of the on-site investigation, and then the overall documentation would have been forwarded to the competent investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's look at paragraph 16 now. In that part of your statement, you deal with the sniping area of Spicasta Stijena, an issue that we heard discussed today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P3 in e-court for a brief moment, specifically page 30. It's page 26 in the binder. Can we have just the one image. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this photograph, do you recognise Sedrenik and Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the left-hand side you see this elevated area with antennae. Can you recognise what it is?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is Grdonj, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. It's an elevation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Grdonj, this elevation was held by who?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: If you mean the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, they were behind this part that is displayed now where the radio tower is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was on the elevation itself?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no one on the elevation itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From this elevation, was it possible to control the area of Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No. It was not possible, because you can see the terrain for yourself. It was rocky. It wasn't forested. And as far as I know, there was no one there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Near Sedrenik, Spicasta Stijena, and Grdonj, was there also Kobilja Glava?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Kobilja Glava is part of a neighbourhood near Vogosca which is a few kilometres away from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the other side -- or, actually, in relation to Spicasta Stijena, where is the area called Sedam Suma?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Sedam Suma was the forested part of Sedrenik, which is no longer there. The trees have been cut down. It's on the right-hand side of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that from Grdonj one could see all of Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Not only Sedrenik but also part of Pionirska Dolina, Kosevo, the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the positions of the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the area of Grdonj and Spicasta Stijena were 20 metres apart?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, I don't know that, because as a policeman, I never came to these positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you know that in the area of Sedrenik there were parts of the 105th Brigade of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I heard of these names, but which territory, which part of the territory was held by them, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you heard that in addition to the fact that the infrastructure and the staff of that brigade were there, there was also the 1st and 2nd Battalion of the 150th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Paragraph 18, please. You speak of the composition of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was stationed in Sedrenik, and you say that basically these were citizens or residents of Sedrenik.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I did not say that the BH Army was stationed at Sedrenik. Rather, I said that on the right and left side of Spicasta Stijena there were one or two trenches that were facing Mrkovici, or, rather, Spicasta Stijena up there, the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what about the members of the Army of Republika Srpska who were on the other side? Where were they from, do you know?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps consisted of people from the areas of Sarajevo and Romanija?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't know at all where these soldiers of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps came from?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No. I never saw a single document that would prove any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you this because in your reports, and today as well, well, you call them Chetniks today, and that's also contained in your reports. And you also called them aggressors. What was your basis for denoting the units of the Army of Republika Srpska in this way?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The statements of these persons themselves on television were such, and to this day you hear statements like that on television, people who introduce themselves as Chetniks. They themselves say that they are Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I wanted to ask you was whether you called all the members of the Army of Republika Srpska Chetniks, and did you call their fire Chetnik fire or aggressor fire, or were these positions of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: It's not only Chetnik fire. At that time they had the support of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which period are we talking about, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To the intent you wanted to draw the attention of the Chamber to the language used by this witness where he says Chetniks, by the way, he corrected himself before the break once in saying giving the different name, you have succeeded in doing that. To the extent it's necessary to further elaborate we'll see, but that point is clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall move on then to paragraph 19. In that paragraph, you say that your estimate was that about 100 civilians were killed by fire coming from Spicasta Stijena. Then in paragraph 20 you say many civilians from Sedrenik were wounded and killed. Their number's around 50 and 100, but this is not exact data. In the Perisic trial --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D445 in e-court now. It's the transcript from that trial. 4556 is the page that we need, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can we have e-court page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It should be page 12. Forty-two, actually. Sorry. That's the right page, and we need lines 17 through 21, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague put a question to you here. I'll read it in English so that you can get the right interpretation. [In English] "Q. I asked you very specifically whether you are aware of any other incidents besides the two that you participated in. Are you aware of any other concrete incident, victim or a colleague of yours who participated in an investigation of a very concrete incident?" And your answer was: "A. I can't remember any." [Interpretation] This is what I'm going to ask you today, and we'll deal with these two incidents as well. Is it correct that you have knowledge, specific knowledge, about two incidents only, two incidents of wounding in Sedrenik, one is Selmanovic, Dervisa, and the second one is Ibrahim Podrug; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: In the police station of Stari Grad at that time, there were about 20 persons who worked as inspectors and who carried out on-site investigations. I'm only one of them. So I don't know how many on-site investigations they carried out. I'm saying that I attended those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid confusion at a later, Mr. Lukic, 4556 transcript page, it's page 43 [realtime transcript read in error "42"] in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At least in my e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now where you earlier wanted to take us to page 42, it's now in our transcript it's by mistake recorded as if I said 42. I said page 43.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you went to the site in Sedrenik, were major offensives of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina underway against the positions of the Army Republika Srpska in Barici and Mrkovici from mid-May until mid-July 1995? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No. I cannot remember whether there were attacks against Spicasta Stijena or, rather, the Mrkovici neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We saw P546 today and we would like to have it called up in e-court again, please. This is a statement made by Mirsad Kuburovic, and you took that statement, right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see from this statement how Ibrahim Podrug was wounded, where the fire came from that wounded him?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This statement was taken from a man who worked as a driver for the emergency medical service who transferred this man who had been lethally wounded. In this Official Note, no reference was made to where the fire had come from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there Serb positions at some points from which they could observe Sedrenik but being below Sedrenik at the same time?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the second paragraph underneath the lettering that says "Statement," this is what was stated, this is what you say: It was stated then that Ibrahim Podrug was wounded by a firearm, that it's an exit-entry wound. The entry wound was at the rear of the thigh muscle while the exit wound was in the area of the groin. As lay persons I can say that it seems to me that Mr. Ibrahim Podrug was standing at a location that was higher than the location where the shooter was, but this is something that forensic experts should be dealing with. The only thing I want to ask you is the following: You correctly registered the information that was provided to you by Mr. Kuburovic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This is Mirsad Kuburovic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that fire was opened against you while you were carrying out your on-site investigation at Sedrenik. You were never wounded at Sedrenik; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How far away is Spicasta Stijena from Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Well, roughly 500 to 700 metres to the last part of those houses that are called the Sedrenik neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now move on to Dervisa Selmanovic's wounding, and we need P548 for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While waiting for that, Mr. Lukic, you I think rightly left a matter to the forensic experts. You said as lay persons I can say that it seems to me that Mr. Ibrahim Podrug was standing at a location that was higher than the location where the shooter was. Now, we leave it in the hands, but what I have -- I'm trying to understand your observation which is not a question. What makes you believe that he was standing when he was shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. That's why I left it for the forensic experts. We don't know whether he was standing or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you say standing higher or lower already assumes a position of standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He can be lying or be seated. I just wondered whether I missed something where you said whether standing was lower or higher where I thought whether he was seated, lying down, et cetera. I have no clue yet. So apart from higher or lower, even whether he was standing. I have no clue in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I couldn't find that clue either in this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. Then I didn't miss anything. Just for me to fully under your -- what you would like to leave to the forensics. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But is your position, Mr. Lukic, that he was standing or do you -- are you open to any other posture that he might have taken until you hear evidence by the observer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm open for anything, Your Honour, but if he -- that gentleman were standing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, but the problem is the experts will not tell us whether he was standing or not. It's an eyewitness only who can tell us whether he was standing, or the position he was in when he was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We cannot find it from the documentation, Your Honour. I tried to find it but I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we're looking at the document which speaks about the wounding of Ms. Dervisa Selmanovic. As you were conducting this on-site investigation, you did not find any of the injured at the scene, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was the neighbours who described the incident for you; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't take any statements from them, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: This was referred to in the record of the on-site investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was stated, that you took statements from them or that you didn't?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The record of the on-site investigation stated that the neighbours were interviewed and they informed the on-site investigation team about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not attend the scene itself, did you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: We reached the house. We didn't attend the spot where Dervisa was wounded because we were afraid that we would come under sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From that spot you photographed the seen which others told you was the place where Dervisa Selmanovic was wounded; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The crime scene examiners photographed the crime scene itself, which had bloodstains for everyone to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't show these photographs to Ms. Selmanovic when you interviewed her; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, we didn't show them to her, because the photographic documentation was already with the investigating judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Based on the story told to you by the neighbours, you produced the report arising from the on-site investigation; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: They were not stories. They were testimonies given by eyewitnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to the part which speaks about the shelling of the area close to the Markale marketplace but before the incidents Markale II happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the document looked at in that context was P550. [In English] This document shouldn't be broadcasted, I think. The Prosecution asked for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on your previous query, the Prosecution did check. It is okay for this document and also P552 to be public exhibits and broadcasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore then the -- the status of this document P550 is public, and P552 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, both documents are public documents from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here you speak about something that happened approximately two months before the incident called Markale II. When the incident described in this document took place, you were not on duty; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I was on duty, but I was not the individual assigned to the on-site investigation duty that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was a colleague of yours; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. The colleague under number 2 was the duty investigator in the Stari Grad station that day. Since the information received was that there were persons killed and children wounded, he asked me to come along and help.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does the documentation state anywhere what the house number was in front of which the shells landed?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The street involved is Dzenetica Cikma Street, and the house numbers 8 through 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You cannot tell at this time what the precise locations were from which this area was fired upon; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: At the time, it was said that the shells were fired from the north, from the area of village of Mrkonjici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement you say that two or three children were harmed or fell victim, and then you say later on that you don't know who fell victim, and then as a third possibility, you say that there may not have been any persons harmed or killed after all.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The on-site investigation team attended the scene on the 26th of June, whereas the incident happened on the 25th of June. In other words, I didn't see the children killed or wounded. We received that information later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that it was said at the time that the shell had come from the north, specifically from the area beyond Spicasta Stijena; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Yes. The village or neighbourhood of Mrkonjic lies behind or beyond Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Between Mrkovici and the place where the shells landed, the forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were deployed; is that right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: From Dzenetica Cikma Street all the way to Spicasta Stijena, there lie the neighbourhoods of Bjelave, Podhrastovo, Sedrenik. I don't know if in that inhabited area there were forces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina deployed or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today we discussed the fact that there were forces deployed in Sedrenik itself. We were able to see that it was a forested area. Is the only place between Spicasta Stijena and the place where the shells landed Sedrenik itself?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't know that there were units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the neighbourhood of Sedrenik. The neighbourhood was such that it comprised stand-alone family homes rather than residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on to the incident where you said three shells landed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I would have one question which I think is close to what you asked the witness. You said that the shell came from the north, and -- let me find it. Specifically from the area beyond Spicasta Stijena, and you said yes. On what basis did you establish the distance, it being beyond Spicasta Stijena?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The record of the on-site investigation does not say that it was ascertained to have been there. It stated that it was approximately the area of Mrkonjici and the area lies beyond Spicasta Stijena.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That still implies an assessment of distance that is beyond Spicasta Stijena and not closer to where the shell fell. Whether it's an area or whether it's a place, it certainly is at a distance not less than the distance to Spicasta Stijena. On what basis was it established that it was that area beyond that sharp rock feature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was stated by ballistics experts who were from the CSB. This was taken from their statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you do not know on what basis they stated that, whether it was an assumption or whether it was on the basis of any specific finding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know on what basis they stated it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Should we make a break now since I'm on the other topic and this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If this would be a suitable moment for a break, we take the break now, and after the witness has left the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you're ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: May we proceed, sir. I would just briefly like to go back to this description of yours, this description that you provided for death sowers. Did you ever see that weapon? Have you ever seen it?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Only in photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is that something special that only the Serb forces had, or is that a machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Well, it's a machine-gun. At first it was only the army of -- I mean the JNA, rather, probably requisitioned the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was this weapon manufactured in the former Yugoslavia or is it an imported weapon?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I think that it was manufactured in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me then that the members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina also had that weapon?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Maybe afterwards in the war if they happened to seize one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your police station, as far as weaponry is concerned, you had 762 automatic rifles; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You also had sniper weapons, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't remember that we had sniper weapons, but we did have semi-automatic rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have M-74 light machine-guns?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't remember, but maybe it was the old machine-gun, M-53. Maybe we had one or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you have NATO rifles?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about the Special Police forces? Did they have NATO rifles?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you find out and what kind of weapon wounded these two persons who were wounded at Sedrenik?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No. Although we looked for it, we were trying to find the ammunition, but we didn't manage to find the weapon or the person who fired the weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you find out that Mrs. Selmanovic, Dervisa Selmanovic, worked in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I took a statement from her. She may have been involved as a cook or something like that, but I don't remember her being involved in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now we are going to discuss the three shells. What was it that you told us? What was established? From which direction did they come?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: The three shells in Dzenetica Cikma or some other shells?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The three shells that you said were fired and you said that they were looking for a target.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Our view is that the shells that fell in Dzenetica Cikma were actually intended for Markale, and I was also doing an on-site investigation when shells were falling from --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat all the names of the streets slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the all the names of the streets and do it slowly so that the interpreters are able to translate. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in the first case it is Dzenetica Cikma. We believed then and we are of the opinion now that this was actually being fired at Markale, because that is where most of the citizens were. On the other hand, I also carried out an on-site investigation, so I was present when in the street Skenderija an on-site investigation was carried out. Hamdija Kresovljakovica is it's name now. And then Branilaca Sarajeva near the municipality of Stari Grad, then the street of Ferhadija near the school of economics of the University of Sarajevo and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please calm down because you're creating the same problem as you did before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you have mentioned now the -- clearly the first street. You then talked about the street Skenderija, and could you repeat what its name is now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hamdija Kresovljakovica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last street you referred to started with Ferhadija. Is that -- could you repeat that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other street is Branilaca Sarajeva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were those all the streets you mentioned or are we still missing one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ferhadija is missing, and the street called Mula Mustafe Baseskije.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These explosions occurred two months before the incident of Markale II; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't have the official record before me. I have the one of the 26th of June, 1995, but I think -- I think that it's before Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That that was a preparation for Markale. That's your assumption, isn't it? It could not have been established through ballistic evidence. There was no evidence that the same weapons were fired. These are just assumptions; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: What we assumed happened in August 1995 as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I shall repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic is asking you the following: If you have not established whether the weapons used in these previous incidents of shelling, then it is just an assumption to say that it was preparation for Markale II, because you would -- because for Markale II, these incidents to be a preparation for Markale II would require that the shells were fired by the same weapons, and if you have been unable to establish that, Mr. Lukic puts to you that, therefore, that must just be an assumption, nothing more, nothing less. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: During the war, did you ever see artillery firing from the city of Sarajevo, that is to say using guns, tanks, or mortars? Artillery of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No, I did not see any of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know and did you know then where artillery pieces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were positioned in the town of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where artillery pieces of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were positioned around the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Again, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I could ask. Did you know about the presence of artillery pieces of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Sarajevo? So irrespective of where they were, did you know that there were artillery pieces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not know. I'm not even sure whether the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina possessed any such heavy weaponry in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So in all your reports, you never took into account the possibility of fire being opened by weapons that were in the possession of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: No. No, we never took into account such a possibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that UNPROFOR reported about incidents when the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina fired at its own population?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: I never heard that officially. Perhaps in chitchat.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 29, you are talking about the first shell that exploded in the street called Skenderija, and you say that a young man who studied political science was killed and that it was close to a secondary school. At that time, in the summer of 1995, were there any students in that school, and were classes going on in that school, or was it members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were stationed in that school? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: At that time and today and before the war this was the Faculty of Political Science, and that is where students were. May I finish? The young man who got killed is from Sedrenik. Later on I met his father. He was 20-something years old, and he had come to enroll in university.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's what I asked you, but probably I misspoke. Because these were the summer months. Certainly there were no classes going on; right?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that there were some lectures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What's the month that we're discussing now?

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: August. But these were not normal times. It wasn't the kind of school that came to exist after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that it's possible that there was a school there and that -- but you don't know for sure that there were classes going on.

utterances.speaker: NEDZIB DJOZO
utterances.text: What is certain is that that was the Faculty of Political Science and that it was students who were there and not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a question. Do you have exact knowledge on classes ongoing in that school in the short time period around the day when the shell -- shelling took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that period of time, that is to say I'm talking about that year, those months, this was the Faculty of Political Science where students went to classes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you there then again. Is that because you assume that when there's a Faculty of Political Science that students will be there, or do you know that classes were held and that students were there in that short weeks around this moment of shelling?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
